newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan, U.S. sign "open skies" accord.
newsitem.headline: Jordan, U.S. sign "open skies" accord.

text.p: Jordan and the United States signed an "open skies" agreement on Sunday which will fully liberalise commercial air services between the two countries, the U.S. embassy said.
It said Jordan was the first country outside Europe to enter into such an agreement with Washington, which lifts restrictions on the number and prices of flights between signatory states.
The accord was signed by Transport Minister Nasser al-Lawzi and U.S. Ambassador Wesley Egan, an embassy statement said.
"Open Skies advances U.S. and Jordanian aviation interests and strengthens the already close and friendly relations between the two countries," it said.

Lawzi told Reuters on Friday the accord would give national carrier Royal Jordanian a key advantage over regional carriers of "flying at any frequency and any number of passengers to any U.S. destination" without prior approval.
It would also make heavily indebted Royal Jordanian more appealing to potential investors in its proposed privatisation programme, he added.
